acceptanceCriteria: Spec requirements (test-validity or appmap domain spec) for actor-role resolution, request-to-ability resolution, inherited rule-set evaluation, the ACTOR-UNAUTHORIZED finding fields, the rejection-assertion exemption, and UNKNOWN for each unresolved link

A first slice that works on a synthetic fixture (JS fixture factory with role:, Rails-style routes plus CanCanCan-style ability rules with inheritance, or a declared project-owned role/ability table if source parsing is out of scope), reproducing the issue's assistant/manager repro as a finding, an authorized pair as clean, and a 403-asserting test as exempt
Finding names the granting rule file:line, the lowest sufficient role and the alternative fixtures; unresolvable inputs yield UNKNOWN with reason
Build log records the supported frameworks, non-goals (other auth libraries, runtime policy) and that no live qualification was run
body: GitHub issue #1115. A browser test logs in as a fixture-seeded user (for example role assistant) and sends a write request (PUT /api/widgets/:id) whose controller action authorizes an ability (authorize! :update, Widget) that only a higher role (manager, which inherits from assistant) holds. Nothing flags it before the run; it shows up as a 403 after a full lane run, and the fix (pick or seed a higher-role user) is found by reading authorization rules by hand. Requested: for each request a test sends under a logged-in fixture actor, (1) resolve the actor role from the fixture builder (a literal role: passed to the user factory, or the factory default); (2) resolve the route to controller#action and the ability it checks; (3) check the role's rule set, including inherited rule sets; (4) report ACTOR-UNAUTHORIZED with role, ability, the granting rule file:line, the lowest role that has the ability, and other fixtures that seed such a role. Advisory, or skipped, when the test deliberately asserts a rejection (401/403/422; see the rejection-anchor work in V1-1737/PR #1101). Today internal/appmap only carries front-end screen permissions (router.go); nothing parses back-end authorization rules, fixture roles or server routes. Any link that can't be resolved (dynamic role, non-literal ability, unknown route) must be reported as UNKNOWN with its reason, never as authorized.
title: test-validity: flag fixture actors whose role is not authorized for the request the test sends (ACTOR-UNAUTHORIZED) (#1115)
